It also records the electricity-price claim as Trump’s assertion; it does not independently verify that claim. A broader account of implementation, affected projects, or energy-price effects would require separate records. The current packet supplies no such records.

frozen_original_identity.title: DOGE Officially Shutters July 4 — Leaves $11 Billion Hole and 300K Lost Federal Jobs

proposal.title: DOGE Temporary Organization Set to Terminate July 4; Service Reported Official Work Ending Over Independence Day 2026
proposal.description_short: The Washington Post reported that DOGE marked what it said was the end of its official work over Independence Day 2026.
proposal.description_medium: Executive Order 14158 set the U.S. DOGE Service Temporary Organization to terminate July 4, 2026. The Washington Post reported on July 6 that the service marked what it said was the end of its official work over Independence Day. The order does not say that other authorities or agency DOGE teams ended.
proposal.description_long: Executive Order 14158, published in the Federal Register on January 29, 2025, renamed the United States Digital Service as the United States DOGE Service and established a temporary organization within it. The order set that temporary organization’s termination date for July 4, 2026, and says its termination does not imply termination, attenuation, or amendment of other authorities or provisions in the order. It also directs agency heads to establish DOGE teams within their agencies. The Washington Post reported on July 6, 2026, that the service marked what it said was the end of its official work over Independence Day and that the temporary organization had been expected to terminate July 4. These sources support a scheduled termination and an attributed report about the service’s statement. They do not establish that every DOGE-related activity across agencies stopped, and they do not support claims about job losses, federal costs, or savings. This description keeps the temporary organization’s scheduled end distinct from broader DOGE activity.

proposal.title: NY Attorney General Petition Alleges $2.823 Million from Iowa Fundraiser Went to Trump Foundation
proposal.description_short: The NY Attorney General’s verified petition alleges the Jan. 28, 2016 Iowa fundraiser raised about $5.6 million; $2.823 million went to Trump Foundation.
proposal.description_medium: The New York Attorney General’s verified petition alleges that the January 28, 2016 Iowa veterans fundraiser raised about $5.6 million and that $2.823 million went to the Trump Foundation. The amounts are allegations in the filing, not findings established by it. This concerns the fundraiser, not the separate later court order.
proposal.description_long: The New York Attorney General’s verified petition identifies a nationally televised veterans fundraiser in Des Moines, Iowa, on January 28, 2016. It alleges that the Trump campaign extensively directed and coordinated the Foundation’s activity around the event, including the timing, recipients, and amounts of disbursements. The petition says the event raised approximately $5.6 million in tax-free donations, of which $2.823 million was contributed to the Trump Foundation; the remainder was donated directly by private donors to veterans’ charity groups. It also says Trump held the fundraiser instead of participating in a televised Republican candidates’ debate, less than one week before the Iowa caucuses. These statements are allegations made in the Attorney General’s petition, not findings established by the filing itself. This description concerns the 2016 fundraiser and alleged transfer; it does not say that the entire $5.6 million went to the Foundation or treat the allegations as a judicial finding.
